quarterly_data.quarter: TeraWulf press release: TeraWulf Expands Contracted Power Capacity at its Muskie (10-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: TeraWulf executed an amended and restated electric service agreement with Kentucky Power, an American Electric Power (AEP) company, increasing contracted power capacity at its Muskie Data Campus in eastern Kentucky from 500 MW to 1 GW. The amendment advances planned delivery of Muskie's second 500 MW phase from 2030 to 2029, subject to Kentucky Public Service Commission approval and Kentucky Power's construction schedule; the first 500 MW phase remains targeted to begin ramping in 2028. Kentucky Power is developing a 765-kV / 345-kV substation connected to the regional transmission network to serve the site, and TeraWulf continues to evaluate the campus's potential to support up to 2 GW over time, subject to additional utility planning, infrastructure and agreements. CEO Paul Prager: 'Customer interest in Muskie has been tremendous, and power availability is central to those conversations'; securing the next 500 MW and moving its planned delivery into 2029 gives TeraWulf greater flexibility to meet prospective customers' deployment needs.
quarterly_data.figure: contracted power capacity at Muskie raised from 500 MW to 1 GW; second 500 MW phase advanced from 2030 to 2029 (subject to Kentucky PSC approval); first 500 MW phase targeted to begin ramping in 2028; potential up to 2 GW over time
